title: Evolution of terrestrial anatomy revealed by a derived stem tetrapod.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: no PMCID, not open access in Europe PMC, no supplement, no text-mined accessions, no NCBI links. Searched Zenodo (7 hits for 'Westlothiana', none from this paper) and Dryad (0 hits). No data file found to open.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything, from the abstract alone: a new anatomical description of one fossil species (Westlothiana lizziae, Early Carboniferous) and phylogenetic analyses. The character matrix and any CT (computed tomography) scans, presumably deposited somewhere such as MorphoBank or MorphoSource, were not located.

a1_downloadable.note: No deposited data found: paper is paywalled, no supplement listing reachable, nothing on Zenodo or Dryad under the DOI or taxon name. Checked repositories, not files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No prediction target. The paper's output is a phylogenetic placement of one species, not a labelled table; any label (e.g. terrestrial vs aquatic) would have to be constructed by inference. Judged from the abstract only.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs would be anatomical character scores (morphological traits coded as 0/1/2 per taxon) or CT scans of a few specimens; neither was located.

a4_units_stated.note: Not applicable / not checkable; morphological characters are categorical codes with no units, and no file was opened.

a5_enough_rows.note: A phylogenetic character matrix for early tetrapods typically holds tens to low hundreds of taxa, far under the ~400-row minimum; the paper's focus is one species. Exact taxon count not seen.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; a character matrix would be kilobytes

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Any ecological label would come from expert anatomical interpretation, and phylogenetic placement is itself the output of a parsimony/Bayesian model fitted to the same characters, so it would be circular.

honest_claim_h3: No ML claim is supportable: this is a single-fossil anatomical description plus a phylogenetic analysis, with no located data table.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use coded skeletal traits of early four-limbed animals to predict whether each species lived on land or in water.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-species anatomical trait codes from the paper's phylogenetic matrix; number of species unknown (matrix not located), likely well under a few hundred.
plain_idea.predict: A land/water lifestyle class, which would itself be an expert interpretation of anatomy rather than a measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Paleontologists could flag ambiguous fossils, but with tens of taxa and expert-derived labels the model would add nothing over the experts.

label_elsewhere.sources: None searched in depth; ecological labels for Paleozoic tetrapods are scattered across individual descriptive papers.
label_elsewhere.why: No large public resource carries this label, so there is no extra training data.

ml_idea: None viable. The only conceivable task (classifying ecology from morphological characters) has tens of rows and expert-derived labels.

effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count taxa in the deposited character matrix (if found on MorphoBank); it will be far under 400.

verdict_reason: Single-fossil paleontology description: no located data deposit, no label column, and a phylogenetic matrix would have tens of taxa, far below the row minimum (Part A1, A2, A5 fail).
